inspection_method: local shallow git clone plus git show; checkout reported Windows filename-length failures for some test fixtures, so source anchors were read through git objects where needed

anchors.why: Identifies the plugin, shows source-file update behavior from query results, global filter guidance, query example, and limit warning.
Confirms plugin id, version, min Obsidian app version, help URL, and desktop/mobile support.
Shows build, lint, markdown lint, test, integration test, local deploy, i18n, circular dependency, and code-docs scripts.
Documents tasks code blocks, filters, global query, query file defaults, presets, grouping, sorting, limits, and query assembly order.
Documents the explain instruction for interpreted dates, booleans, global query, file defaults, grouping, sorting, and limits.
Documents optional global filter behavior and the need to restart after changes.
Documents status symbol, name, next symbol, type, unknown status handling, and custom status behavior.
Documents urgency score formula and limitations such as ignored status/dependencies.
Documents that JavaScript expressions in query blocks require enabling and trust in vault contents.
Shows JavaScript in Tasks queries disabled by default and stored in vault-local app storage.
Generates human-readable descriptions of parsed queries, filters, groups, sorters, layout, and limits.
Parses Obsidian cached list items and file lines while handling stale cache line-number mismatch.
Contains approved samples for documentation-driven behavior checks; some paths exceed default Windows checkout limits.

known_limits: Task query results, statuses, and urgency are activation/workbench signals, not reviewed knowledge or truth confidence.
JavaScript query expressions require explicit trust and should remain disabled by default in VAKS-like flows.
Local Windows checkout produced filename-length errors, so path-length lint matters for source snapshots.
